item.text:
# 1B.1 Research Note: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in 2024

Overall read: **mixed, leaning de-escalatory on Ukraine and Gaza, but with clear conventional brinkmanship and leverage politics in July 2024**. I found no direct 2024 evidence of Erdoğan pursuing nuclear escalation; the evidence is about whether he tried to lower broader war risk or used conflict rhetoric for leverage.

| Direction | Accepted claim | Source | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Supports 1B.1 | Erdoğan said Türkiye had worked “since day one” to end the Russia-Ukraine war, wanted diplomacy to have a chance, and supported Ukraine’s territorial integrity while warning NATO should not become a party to the war. This is direct de-escalation language. | **“Global peace and stability cannot be addressed without a lasting solution to the Israel-Palestine issue”**; Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications; 2024-07-12; https://www.tccb.gov.tr/en/news/542/152994/-global-peace-and-stability-cannot-be-addressed-without-a-lasting-solution-to-the-israel-palestine-issue- | `1B.1` |
| Supports 1B.1 | Erdoğan said Türkiye was ready to act as a guarantor and push for a ceasefire and lasting peace in Gaza, framing peace as the route to regional stability. | **“Global peace and stability cannot be addressed without a lasting solution to the Israel-Palestine issue”**; Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications; 2024-07-12; https://www.tccb.gov.tr/en/news/542/152994/-global-peace-and-stability-cannot-be-addressed-without-a-lasting-solution-to-the-israel-palestine-issue- | `1B.1` |
| Supports 1B.1 | Erdoğan said Lebanon’s security and regional peace depended on a Gaza ceasefire and that stronger security cannot come from more bloodshed or civilian massacres. This is a clear anti-escalation argument. | **“Lebanon’s security cannot be assessed separate from the region’s stability”**; Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications; 2024-12-18; https://www.iletisim.gov.tr/english/haberler/detay/lebanons-security-cannot-be-assessed-separate-from-the-regions-stability | `1B.1` |
| Cuts against 1B.1 | Erdoğan said Turkey might “enter Israel” as it had Libya and Nagorno-Karabakh, in a defense-industry speech. That is not nuclear escalation, but it is overt military brinkmanship and escalation rhetoric used for leverage. | **“Erdogan says Turkey might enter Israel to help Palestinians”**; Reuters via VOA; 2024-07-28; https://www.voanews.com/a/erdogan-says-turkey-might-enter-israel-to-help-palestinians/7716248.html | `1B.1` |
| Cuts against 1B.1, mixed | Erdoğan said Turkey would not approve NATO cooperation with Israel until there was comprehensive and sustainable peace in Palestine. That is a conditional veto posture: peace-linked in form, but also an exercise of alliance leverage rather than a clean de-escalation move. | **“Erdogan says Turkey will not approve NATO attempts to cooperate with Israel”**; Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications / Reuters syndication; 2024-07-12; https://www.iletisim.gov.tr/english/haberler/detay/erdogan-says-turkey-will-not-approve-nato-attempts-to-cooperate-with-israel | `1B.1` |

## Search gap

I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence that Erdoğan pursued nuclear escalation, nuclear signaling, or nuclear brinkmanship. The available evidence is instead:
- pro-de-escalation on Ukraine and Gaza,
- conditional peace rhetoric,
- and one clear piece of conventional military brinkmanship toward Israel.
